subject: Request: non-standard accelerator + transient surge concession for Helix Labs
body:
---Original Message---
From: Bryan Cole <bryan.cole@helixlabs.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Helix Labs Sales Ops <salesops@helixlabs.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask: H100 mix + transient surge credits

Hi Priyom / Jonas,

Quick note from our infra team after the sizing workshop: Helix is ready to commit to a 12-month Dedicated capacity contract, but we need two concessions to get the internal approvals across the finish line:

1) Guaranteed access to an H100 accelerator family for 60% of baseline capacity (we can accept a smaller number of variants but need H100-equivalent perf for our initial model suite).
2) A transient surge credit pool equal to 20% of monthly baseline for the first three months (we anticipate peak-during-onboarding traffic).

Also asking if Redwood can cap overage rates for burst usage at the first-month rate in case we exceed the allocation in initial weeks. I attached a short demand forecast and proposed terms for context.

Bryan
VP Infrastructure, Helix Labs

---

On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 12:05 PM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Bryan Cole <bryan.cole@helixlabs.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask: H100 mix + transient surge credits

Thanks Bryan — this is clear and reasonable to discuss. Quick notes:
- Baseline H100 blend for 60% is non-standard but feasible; depends on pool availability and lead time.
- Transient surge credits of 20% for three months is something we can model from a billing perspective, but it requires approval on both the burst-capacity policy and an override to our standard overage pricing.

Jonas — looping you and Lauren for exec signoff on the transient-credit allowance and to confirm whether an H100 mix guarantee can be scoped as a preferred-sku reservation rather than absolute dedicated hardware. I attached the Helix forecast.

Next step: can we get a quick decision so I can lock this into their SOW? Helix expects a signed SOW by next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

---

On Sat, Apr 3, 2027 at 08:30 AM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Dedicated capacity ask: H100 mix + transient surge credits

Team — forwarding Helix ask. Summary of decision points we need from Deal Desk / Execs:
1) Approve preferred-sku reservation language: allow Helix to pin a percentage of their commitment to H100-class instances (we'd provide compatible fallback SKUs only when absolutely necessary). This is effectively a high-priority allocation, not physical exclusive hardware.
2) Approve a three-month transient surge credit equal to 20% of baseline usage applied as pre-funded burst credits to avoid punitive overage in onboarding months. Accounting: this is treated as a one-time credit drawdown against committed value.
3) Cap burst overage price at the contracted month-1 rate for any usage during the first 60 days, thereafter revert to standard overage tiers.

Risk notes: high demand periods could make H100 preference breachable; fallback must be automatic and transparent to Helix. The credit reduces initial ARR realization and sets a billing precedent for future strategic deals.

Suggested compromise to present to Helix if needed: 50% H100 preferred baseline (instead of 60%), and 15% transient credits for three months with a conditional review at 45 days (empirical trigger to extend credits if onboarding metrics show continued spike).

Asking for a short yes/no + any redlines today so Priyom can finalize the SOW draft.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

---

On Sat, Apr 3, 2027 at 14:15 Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Dedicated capacity ask: H100 mix + transient surge credits

Jonas / Lauren — I spoke with Finance and Legal this morning. My read: we can approve the following with exec signoff (conditions below):

- Approve preferred-sku reservation up to 55% of baseline as a contractual "preferred allocation". Fallback SKUs must be documented with explicit performance deltas; Helix must accept a degradation SLA if we invoke fallback.
- Approve transient surge credits up to 15% of baseline for the first 90 days. Credits will be drawn from the customer's committed invoice and amortized over first 2 months to smooth recognition.
- Cap overage rate at month-1 pricing for the initial 60-day window. After that, standard overage rates apply.

Conditions: Helix signs the SOW with a minimum 12-month committed spend at the proposed tier and accepts a 30-day notice window for any hardware-class fallback. Any deviation from the fallback SLA will require a separate approval.

If the customer pushes for 20% credits and 60% H100, escalate to me + Lauren and we can bring this to the Deal Desk exec call.

Marissa
VP, Partnerships & Strategic Deals — Redwood Inference

---

On Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 10:00 AM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Bryan Cole <bryan.cole@helixlabs.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Helix Labs Sales Ops <salesops@helixlabs.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity ask: H100 mix + transient surge credits

Bryan — thanks for the clarity and the forecast file. We want to move quickly to get you into production. Here's what we can commit to today (subject to SOW language we will send):

1) Preferred-sku reservation: 55% of baseline capacity can be designated as an H100-preferred allocation. This is a preferred allocation (not physically isolated hardware). We will document fallback SKUs and expected perf impact; fallback may be invoked during capacity pressure with 30 days' notice.

2) Transient surge credits: we will extend a 15% transient credit pool applied across the first 90 days. Credits will be applied to your committed invoice and amortized as described by our Finance team.

3) Overage cap: overage charges during the first 60 days will be billed at month-1 rates. After 60 days, standard overage tiers apply.

If Helix wants to push to 60% H100 or 20% transient credits, we'll need to escalate to the Deal Desk exec rota and document the business rationale; please let us know if you want us to start that process.

Action items: Priyom will update the SOW and terms matrix and circulate for signature by EOD Tue. Bryan — once you ack, we'll issue the SOW and a short addendum capturing the preferred-allocation and transient-credit mechanics.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Helix_Demand_Forecast_Q3.xlsx, Requested_Terms_Summary.docx, SOW_draft_v2.pdf
